_README: SCOPED FACT EXTENSION for japanforamericans — created 2026-09-16. This is NOT a replacement for facts.json. It covers only the fields the 10 new depth articles need (article-list.json slugs listed under each section). The standard facts-template.json has no fields at this granularity: when_to_go carries 3 fields, getting_around.intercity_rail is a single field, and connectivity has no IC-card field at all. That schema gap is WHY the jr-pass-math, ic-card-setup and seasonal-timing vein pieces measured THIN (4,305 / 4,294 / 821 corpus words) — the facts were never asked for. Reconcile the panel replies into facts.json as NEW keys; never overwrite an existing key or a human dispute ruling.
_fact_field_shape: Every FACT uses { value, source_url, status, notes }. status is one of: verified (source_url MUST be the official page actually checked) | agreed_stable | verify_recommended | serve_live. Never invent a source_url. Prices and app behaviour here are VOLATILE — default them to verify_recommended, never verified, unless you genuinely checked the official page.

_meta.audience: US passport holders, flying from US hubs, thinking in USD
_meta.locale_note: facts.json _meta.locale governs units; keep yen as the native figure and let the site convert

rail_passes._why: The site's own swamp note already says 'the Pass price hike means a simple Tokyo-Kyoto round trip no longer breaks even' — but facts.json holds no price at all, so that claim cannot be written. These fields make the break-even argument writable.

national_pass_variants.notes: 7 / 14 / 21-day, ordinary and Green. Give the CURRENT yen price of each. Six figures.

national_pass_price_change.notes: The most recent price change: old price, new price, effective date. This is the fact the whole break-even argument turns on.

nozomi_mizuho_rule.notes: Are the fastest Tokaido/Sanyo services covered by the national pass, and is there a paid supplement option? State the rule, not an opinion.

tokyo_kyoto_one_way_cost.notes: Shinkansen Tokyo→Kyoto, ordinary car, reserved seat, one way, in yen. The single number a reader needs to do the maths.

break_even_trips.notes: How many Tokyo-Kyoto-equivalent legs a 7-day national pass must cover to pay for itself, at current prices.

regional_passes_core.notes: The 3-5 regional passes that actually matter to a first-timer on a Tokyo/Kyoto/Osaka route. For each: name, issuer, duration, current yen price, what it covers, what it does NOT cover.

where_to_buy.notes: Online in advance vs at a Japanese station: is there still a price difference, and what does activation require (passport, temporary visitor stamp)?

eligibility.notes: Who may buy the national pass — the 'temporary visitor' status rule, and anything that excludes a US visitor.

ic_cards._why: facts.json holds exactly 3 IC-card mentions, all generic ('Suica/Pasmo IC card', 'IC card works'). The site's swamp note already flags 'app-based with quirks for foreign phones' — these fields make that writable.

card_types_and_interop.notes: Suica / Pasmo / Icoca and the national interoperability rule — where a Tokyo card does and does not work.

physical_card_availability.notes: Are unregistered physical Suica/Pasmo cards currently sold to visitors, or is availability still restricted? State the current position and the date it applies to.

welcome_suica.notes: Tourist-specific card: what it is, validity period, where sold, whether the balance is refundable.

mobile_suica_ios.notes: Adding Suica/Pasmo to Apple Wallet on a US-bought iPhone: is a Japanese Apple ID or App Store region needed, which region setting matters, and what the actual steps are.

mobile_topup_us_cards.notes: Which US-issued cards can top up a mobile Suica in Apple Wallet, and which are refused. This is the single most common American failure point — be specific about card networks.

android_limitation.notes: Why a US Android phone generally cannot run mobile Suica (Osaifu-Keitai hardware), and what the workaround is if any.

balance_limits_and_refund.notes: Maximum stored balance, top-up increments, and how/whether a visitor can refund a remaining balance on departure (and any fee).

day_passes_tokyo.notes: Tokyo Metro 24/48/72-hour tourist passes: current yen prices and what they cover (Metro only vs Toei).

day_passes_kyoto.notes: Kyoto bus/subway day passes: current yen prices, coverage, and whether the bus-only pass still exists.

when_ic_beats_pass.notes: The practical rule of thumb for a first-timer: at what level of daily travel does a day pass beat pay-as-you-go on an IC card?

seasonal._why: facts.json covers seasons at the level of 'spring is mild, avoid Golden Week'. That supports one article — the corpus has exactly one (best-time-to-visit-japan, 821 words). Six articles need per-event specifics.

sakura_peak_windows.notes: Typical full-bloom window for Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka, as date ranges with the caveat that it shifts yearly. Name the official forecast body.

sakura_booking_lead.notes: How far ahead accommodation in Kyoto/Tokyo realistically needs booking for the bloom window.

koyo_peak_windows.notes: Autumn foliage peak windows for Tokyo, Kyoto and the Japanese Alps, as date ranges.

golden_week_dates.notes: The constituent public holidays and their fixed dates, plus how the run-of-days forms. Fixed dates are stable; the exact run varies by year.

golden_week_effects.notes: What actually changes for a visitor: domestic rail and flight demand, accommodation pricing, which attractions and businesses close.

obon_dates_and_effects.notes: The mid-August observance: typical dates, and what it does to rail, domestic flights and regional closures.

new_year_closures.notes: Shogatsu — the end-December to early-January period. What closes and for how long. This is the closure period Americans most often walk into unaware.

public_holidays_list.notes: The national public holidays with their dates or rules. Name the official source.

tsuyu_rainy_season.notes: Typical start and end of the rainy season for Honshu vs Okinawa, and what it means in practice (all-day rain, or humid with showers?).

typhoon_season.notes: Peak typhoon months, which regions are most exposed, and the practical disruption pattern for rail and flights.

summer_heat.notes: Typical August temperature and humidity in Tokyo/Kyoto, and whether heat is a genuine itinerary constraint.

winter_snow_regions.notes: Where snow is reliable (Hokkaido, Tohoku, the Japan Sea side), and the months.

winter_low_season.notes: Is winter genuinely cheaper and quieter outside New Year and ski areas? Give the pattern, not a slogan.
